GitHub Copilot now names custom tools in usage reports. Your quality check is still missing.

What changed: GitHub's Oct. 22 update replaces generic buckets with configured names for custom skills, agents, MCP servers, slash commands and plugins in eligible usage reports. Each breakdown now shows up to 25 entries, up from five.

What it does: eligible teams can see which internal tools are getting used. Interaction counts are unchanged. These are adoption trends, not exact accounting or output-quality scores.

Why builders should care: a tool can be busy and still produce work you cannot use. On Tech Thursday, the CLI-connected image batch executed, but the host rejected its visual quality. Running was not the same as ready.

Try this week:
1. Pick one existing custom tool with a clear, non-sensitive name, not a file path.
2. If you have report access, check its usage trend after the update.
3. Inspect five outputs yourself. Mark accepted or rejected, with one reason each.
4. Change one instruction and inspect another five before expanding the workflow.

Access requires an eligible enterprise or organization role with View Copilot Metrics, plus the usage metrics policy enabled. Client/version coverage matters; prompt mode, the app and ACP require CLI 1.0.97+, and the SDK requires v1.0.21+. Telemetry can undercount. Earlier report days stay unchanged.

The signal: AI workflows need an operating loop, not just a successful tool call.

Save this for your next agent workflow review.

slides.openai_prompt: Create a cinematic Layer8Culture visual in a deep black environment with electric blue accent lighting, premium creator-tech atmosphere, late-night builder energy, documentary realism, human-centered AI themes, Black tech futurism, minimal composition, strong negative space, warm practical lighting, and high contrast. Vary the composition from post to post so the feed does not repeat — the SCENE SPECIFICS for THIS post decide the subject. Draw from a range of premium looks (do NOT default to the same person-at-a-desk shot every time), for example: a confident Black creator/host presenting direct-to-camera; a close detail of premium creator gear (mic, stream deck, dark walnut desk, the standalone 8 motif on a hoodie or mug); an over-the-shoulder build session; an abstract Afrofuturistic tech or data-visualization environment with glowing electric-blue nodes and grids; or an atmospheric branded studio space. Recurring brand cues when a scene fits: a blank neon sign panel on the wall (an unlit, lettering-free glowing panel - do NOT render any text or letters), the standalone 8 motif, a bookshelf washed in blue accent lighting. When a person appears they are a confident Black creator, engaged and intentional, never anonymous side profiles. The image should feel like a premium technology documentary and creative studio brand. COMPOSITION FOR TYPOGRAPHY: leave the LOWER-LEFT / lower third of the frame as clean, uncluttered negative space (a dark, simple area with no faces, fine detail, or busy elements there) so a branded headline can be composited over it. EDITORIAL CTA ADD-ON: a quiet archival object worth returning to. SCENE: square 1:1 close crop of one closed premium black field notebook standing upright at far upper right, with a single Electric Blue #0047FF fabric bookmark visible and no lettering anywhere. A narrow warm practical catches the page edges against Deep Navy Glow #050A1A. No desk portrait, screen, contact sheet, counter or rail. Most of the frame is clean black negative space, especially lower-left and lower third, for the composited save CTA. Avoid generic startup office, bright corporate lighting, cheap gamer RGB, cluttered composition, cartoon props, excessive sci-fi armor, robots, fake hologram overload, random neon colors, copyrighted franchise references, garbled screen text, random figurines, tripod-mounted monitors, makeshift setups, rendered text, signage lettering, and garbled typography.

text:
AI image workflows: where does yours break?

On Tech Thursday, the CLI-connected image batch completed. The look still wasn't there. Today's carousel separates tool activity from work you can use.

Reply with one: GETTING IT TO RUN or GETTING IT RIGHT.

visual.headline: RUNS. BUT IS IT RIGHT?
visual.subtext: Reply: getting it running or getting it right?
